choices.D: Equal to the distance from the center to the chord

flags: Uses the degenerate-chord convention at tangency; a tangent does not determine a chord with two distinct endpoints.

question: When a line is tangent to a circle, what is the chord length?
solution: Tangency gives only 1 common point. If this point is treated as a degenerate chord with coincident endpoints, its length is \(0\), giving choice A. Under the definition requiring two distinct endpoints, a tangent determines no chord, so A is conditional on the degenerate-chord convention.
